market_scan.market_size_text: The value pool is mineral recovery inside the ~$23B/yr global mineral processing equipment market, but the real prize is recovered metal: a 1% recovery uplift on a large copper concentrator is worth roughly $5-15M/yr in extra revenue — far more than the equipment cost. Liberation/recovery improvements target flotation plants and leach operations within the same comminution-adjacent spend (~$10-15B/yr on crushing/grinding equipment plus separation). Demand is amplified by declining ore grades industry-wide, which forces finer grinding and makes liberation the bottleneck of recovery.

regions.Africa: ~$3-4B/yr incl. Middle East (~15%; copper/cobalt/gold growth, ~10% CAGR)

market_scan.target_customers_text: Same customer base as ore weakening — hard-rock concentrators and leach operations, ~3,000-5,000 sites of the ~15,000 facilities in ICMM's dataset — but the value case differs: recovery uplift pays best on high-value ores (gold, copper, PGM, refractory and low-grade deposits where every recovery point matters). Large concentrators monetise +1% recovery immediately; refractory-gold and heap-leach operators are a particularly receptive niche; small mines need simple bolt-on units. Sales motion is via metallurgical testwork → plant trial, typically 1-3 year adoption cycles.

Large: ~200-400 concentrators (>10 Mt/y; majors, high revenue per recovery point)
Small: ~3,000+ sites (<1 Mt/y; heap-leach and gravity gold)

market_scan.players_text: Recovery performance is today delivered by the same concentrated OEM tier (Metso, FLSmidth, Weir — #1 positions in flotation/classification) plus reagent/leaching specialists; incumbents optimise recovery inside conventional flowsheets rather than changing ore breakage physics. No commercial liberation-enhancing pre-treatment supplier exists: the emerging field (Nottingham/e2v MicroHammer microwave pilots; SELFRAG high-voltage pulse machines with JKMRC/Newcrest testwork showing selective grain-boundary breakage) is pre-commercial, leaving the liberation pre-treatment space open.
players: Flotation cells, classifiers/cyclones, regrind mills, hydrometallurgy — recovery via conventional flowsheet optimisation; strong aftermarket lock-in
top 3 ~35-50% of relevant equipment; Metso #1 flotation/filtration

Separation, leaching, thickening, specialist recovery equipment

Liberation-enhancing pre-treatment: pulse fragmentation, microwave pilots, sensor-based pre-concentration
regulation: Targets 10% domestic extraction / 40% processing by 2030 and defines strategic recycling/recovery benchmarks — recovery-maximising technology aligns with EU resource-efficiency objectives and can ease project permitting narratives.
EU Industrial Emissions Directive / MIN BREF
BAT conclusions cover beneficiation/recovery efficiency and specific consumption indicators; better liberation at coarser grind reduces energy AND reagent/water intensity, supporting compliance.
EU ETS + Energy Efficiency Directive Art. 11 audits
Coarser-grind-for-equal-liberation cuts grinding energy; audited energy savings plus avoided metal losses both improve the economics regulators increasingly scrutinise.
Tailings regulations (EU Extractive Waste Directive; GISTM global standard)
Higher recovery = less metal and sulphide to tailings; post-Brumadinho GISTM compliance pressure favours technologies reducing tailings volumes and sulphide content.
Australia Safeguard Mechanism / ICMM net-zero commitments
Declining grades raise energy per tonne of metal; recovery uplift lowers CO2 per unit metal — supports decarbonisation plans of majors committed to net zero.
EMF/RF safety: CISPR 11/EN 55011 ISM + EU Directive 2013/35/EU
Microwave units require shielding to ISM leakage limits (915 MHz/2.45 GHz) and worker EMF limits — engineering requirement, not a licensing barrier.

technologies.name: Fine grinding to liberation size (incumbent)
technologies.how: Ball/SAG mills grind ore until valuable minerals are liberated; recovery is then achieved by flotation, gravity or leaching.
technologies.performance: Grinding ~40% of mine energy (US DOE); typical BWi 10-20 kWh/t; liberation typically requires P80 of 75-300 um, finer for low-grade/complex ores.
technologies.limits: Random bulk breakage liberates poorly at coarse sizes; overgrinding creates slimes that depress flotation/gravity recovery — the trade-off the hypothesis relaxes.

technologies.name: Flotation + regrind circuits (incumbent recovery method)
technologies.how: Rougher/scavenger flotation with regrind of middlings to recover locked particles.
technologies.performance: Typical sulphide Cu recovery ~85-90%, gold ~85-95%; regrind adds several kWh/t.
technologies.limits: Cannot recover values locked at grain boundaries below grind size; recovery gains cost disproportionate energy and capital — microwave cracks along grain boundaries instead.

technologies.name: Roasting / pressure oxidation (refractory ores)
technologies.how: Thermal or autoclave oxidation of pyrite/arsenopyrite or carbonaceous matter to expose encapsulated gold before leaching.
technologies.performance: Enables >90-98% recovery on double-refractory ores but is highly energy- and capex-intensive (autoclaves cost $100M+).
technologies.limits: Only economic at large scale; high emissions. Microwave roasting achieved >98% Au recovery in lab at lower specific energy than conventional roasting — a substitute/add-on niche.

technologies.name: HPGR for heap-leach liberation
technologies.how: HPGR micro-cracking improves permeability and exposes mineral surfaces before heap leaching.
technologies.performance: Documented leach-kinetics and recovery improvements on gold/copper heap leach; ~1.5-4 kWh/t for the HPGR stage.
technologies.limits: Mechanical cracks are less selective than grain-boundary fracture; benefit limited to leachable ores — microwave targets the same micro-crack mechanism more selectively.

technologies.name: High-voltage pulse fragmentation (SELFRAG)
technologies.how: Sub-microsecond discharges fragment ore preferentially along grain boundaries while immersed in water.
technologies.performance: ~1-3 kWh/t for pre-weakening; lab/plant testwork shows coarser liberation and cleaner mineral surfaces than mechanical comminution.
technologies.limits: Low throughput, wet processing, niche adoption; microwave achieves comparable grain-boundary selectivity dry and continuously at demonstrated 10-150 t/h scale.

technologies.name: Microwave pre-treatment (state of the art — the hypothesis technology)
technologies.how: Selective microwave heating of high-dielectric-loss phases generates intergranular cracks at mineral grain boundaries, liberating values at coarser sizes before mechanical grinding.
technologies.performance: Porphyry Cu ore at ~2 kWh/t: equivalent liberation at 40-70 um coarser grind; +~1% Cu flotation recovery or +30-60 um coarser grind at equal recovery. Free-milling gold ore: BWi -18.5%, gravity gold recovery 28%→40%. Refractory concentrates: leach recovery 74%→>90-98% in lab studies.
technologies.limits: Gains depend on dielectric/mineralogical contrast between valuable and gangue phases; recovery uplift of ~1% on porphyry ores is near the detection limit of flotation testwork; no commercial installation yet.

tech_baseline.why_better_text: Incumbents buy liberation with energy — grinding finer until values are exposed — which simultaneously destroys recovery via slimes and locked middlings. Microwave pre-treatment fractures ore preferentially AT grain boundaries, so values are liberated ~40-70 um coarser: the same recovery at lower energy, less overgrinding, and better downstream flotation/gravity/leach performance. The economics are powerful because recovery gains monetise directly as metal revenue (a +1% recovery point is worth several $M/yr on a large concentrator) rather than merely saving cost, and lab evidence shows order-of-magnitude larger effects on free-milling gold (28%→40% gravity recovery) and refractory ores (74%→>90% leach recovery) — niches where the mechanism is strongest.
key_assumptions: Equivalent mineral liberation achievable at ~40-70 um coarser grind after ~0.3-2 kWh/t microwave treatment (measured, Nottingham pilot + MLA analysis)
~+1% Cu flotation recovery demonstrated at pilot-relevant doses; statistically hard to confirm but worth ~$5-15M/yr on a large concentrator (measured, Batchelor et al.)
Free-milling gold gravity recovery improved 28%→40% after microwave pre-treatment; BWi -18.5% (measured, lab scale)
Refractory gold leach recovery 74%→>90-98% via microwave pre-treatment/roasting at lower specific energy than conventional roasting (measured, lab scale)
Recovery benefit requires dielectric/textural contrast between valuable and gangue minerals; ores with unfavourable textures show modest liberation gains (measured — key ore-selection risk)

sources.claim: Porphyry Cu: equivalent liberation at 50-60 um coarser grind; ~+1% Cu recovery or +30 um coarser at equal recovery (15 kW, ~2 kWh/t)
Pilot scale: equivalent liberation 40-70 um coarser at 0.3-3 kWh/t; 150 t/h system, ~300 t treated under power
Free-milling gold ore: crushing strength -31.2%, BWi -18.5%, gravity gold recovery improved ~28%→40%
Double refractory gold: microwave roasting → ~94% organic carbon removal, >98% Au cyanide recovery, lower specific energy than conventional roasting
Refractory gold concentrate: microwave pre-treatment lifted leach recovery from ~74% to >90%
Mechanism: shear stresses highest at grain boundaries of heated particles in microwave-transparent matrix → intergranular fracture and enhanced liberation
MicroHammer: heats/expands copper grains so they split from host rock; >20% extraction energy reduction, production +~1/3
